newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-New Sydney airport environment study seen '97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-New Sydney airport environment study seen '97.

text.p: The approval of a full environmental impact study on a planned second international airport for Australia's largest city, Sydney, would be made in earlier 1997, transport minister John Sharp said on Friday.
"We hope to be able to have the environmental impact study approved by late March or early April next year," Sharp said after giving a speech to the aviation press club.
The govenment is considering two sites to have its second airport, Bagerys Creek and Holdsworthy, both in Sydney's west.
Sharp said there would then be public consultation followed by a cabinet decision.

"Cabinet needs to make a decison on which way it goes, whether it goes to Badgery Creek, which is our first priority or whether it goes to Holsworthy, you will get a decision in regard to this will in calendar 1997," Sharp said.
Sharp said work on the proposed new airport would start in late 1998, and the construction of an airport is expected to take four years to complete.
"I would hope that we would see work commencing on that in late 1998 and depending on how things work it would probably take four years from that point forward for it to be completed," he said.
The second airport was orginally planned to open in time to deal with the expected influx of foreign arribvals for the 2000 Olympic Games in Sydney.
"We are determined to have a second airport, it is very important to have that," he said.
Sydney's existing airport is Australia's busiest domestic and international gateway but has a night curfew due to noise pollution and has a restriction of 80 flight movements each hour.
